title: Subdomain takeover: `shm-playground.playticorp.com` CNAMEs to an unregistered GitHub Pages account
vulnerability_information:
`shm-playground.playticorp.com` still publishes a CNAME to `playtika.github.io`. The GitHub account
`playtika` **does not exist**, and no Pages site is served at `playtika.github.io`, so any GitHub user
who registers the name `playtika` and publishes a repository called `playtika.github.io` will have
their content served on `https://shm-playground.playticorp.com/` — under a valid TLS certificate, on
a `playticorp.com` origin. Playtika does not need to change anything in DNS for this to work, because
the record already points at GitHub.

## Evidence

**1. The CNAME is still published.**

```
$ dig +short shm-playground.playticorp.com CNAME
playtika.github.io.
$ dig +short playtika.github.io A
185.199.108.153
185.199.109.153
185.199.110.153
185.199.111.153        # GitHub Pages anycast
```

**2. The host is answered by GitHub, and GitHub has no site for it.**

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -D- https://shm-playground.playticorp.com/
HTTP/2 302
server: GitHub.com
location: https://github.com/pages/auth?nonce=...&page_id=48972994&path=Lw

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://playtika.github.io/
404
```

The `page_id` in the redirect is GitHub's own record for this custom domain — GitHub is still the
edge for `shm-playground.playticorp.com` and there is no site behind it.

**3. The account name is unregistered.**

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.github.com/users/playtika
404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://github.com/playtika
404
```

Control: a random, definitely-nonexistent owner (`zzqqxx-nonexist-8888.github.io`) returns the same
404, while a real owner with no Pages site (`github.github.io`) also 404s but `github.com/github`
returns 200 — which is exactly how the two cases are told apart. `github.com/playtika` returning 404
means the name can be claimed.

**4. GitHub is still terminating TLS for the Playtika hostname.**

```
$ echo | openssl s_client -connect shm-playground.playticorp.com:443 \
      -servername shm-playground.playticorp.com | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates
subject=CN=shm-playground.playticorp.com
issuer=C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=YR2
notBefore=Sep 19 09:57:49 2026 GMT
notAfter=Dec 18 09:57:48 2026 GMT
```

GitHub only issues a Pages certificate for a custom domain after a Pages site has claimed it, so this
record was serving a Playtika-owned Pages site until the account behind it disappeared. The domain was
never verified under a GitHub account Playtika still controls (`github.com/playtika` is free), which is
why nothing on GitHub's side blocks a third party from claiming it now.

## Steps to reproduce the takeover (not performed)

1. Register the GitHub username `playtika`.
2. Create the repository `playtika/playtika.github.io` with an `index.html`.
3. Add `shm-playground.playticorp.com` as the custom domain of that Pages site.
4. GitHub then serves the attacker's `index.html` at `https://shm-playground.playticorp.com/`.

I have **not** registered the name, published anything, or created any account. If you want a
confirmed takeover rather than a passive one, I will do steps 1–4 on a benign page with no data
collection, send the screenshot and timestamp, and release the username immediately afterwards —
please confirm you want that and I will coordinate the window with you first.
